item: R101: quarantined articles leave the keyword figures, the language series and the equilibrium lever
key_paths: src/analytics/quarantine_scope.py; src/analytics/store.py; src/analytics/quarantine_job.py; src/analytics/columnar.py; src/analytics/queries.py; src/analytics/supergroup_rising.py; src/analytics/supergroup_stats.py; src/database/snapshots.py; src/scheduler/equilibrium.py; src/backup/merge.py; src/analytics/day_counts.py; src/monitoring/integrity.py; src/monitoring/rollup_benchmark.py; src/analytics/keyword_fold.py; src/analytics/keyword_growth.py; src/analytics/quarantine_transition.py; src/database/session.py; src/api/main.py; tests/test_quarantine_leaves_keyword_figures.py; tests/test_quarantine_carry.py
summary: One slice per R101 (PRH-06/D22): one filter (quarantine_scope.not_quarantined, an index-only NOT IN on idx_article_quarantined) shared by the keyword counters (index_article skips a quarantined article; the job's stamp subtracts its mentions in the same commit and bumps the corpus epoch; reconcile/backfill filter), the keyword_daily rollup build and tail refresh and their parity probe, the day_counts store (rebuild, fold and stale-day read), the integrity counter-drift check, the rollup benchmark's live side, the keyword fold (moves a quarantined article's rows without moving the counters), the keyword hover stats, the vocabulary growth curve, every live fallback that stands in for the rollup (top_terms, trending, trend, the supergroup sums), the restore carry delta, article_counts_by_language and corpus_language_shares. furniture_share measured first: unchanged (the qualification path already drops quarantined ids and never reads these aggregates). Cost on a 1M-mention synthetic corpus, 10% quarantined: windowed read 130 to 147 ms (same covering index), a 5k-keyword reconcile slice 23 to 45 ms, the day_counts per-day read 3.4 to 9 ms because ix_mention_date_keyword no longer covers it (an index extension is proposed as a follow-up). A one-time upgrade step brings a store written before 0.5.1 into line: init_db only bumps the corpus epoch and opens the counter deferral (counts read estimated); the start-up upkeep, after the store is queryable, then recomputes the counters of every keyword a quarantined article mentions (idempotent, so a failed attempt cannot double-count) in one commit with the marker; 2.8 s on a 1M-mention synthetic store, 23 s on 7.2M. A double stamp in a race subtracts once (conditional UPDATE under the write lock). 10 of 14 new tests red on main. Not in scope and still counting quarantined articles: other per-article-set mention readers (bulletin coverage, the maintenance one-time counter backfill, which the next reconcile repairs) salvage stand-in articles stamped outside the quarantine job, the fold's frequency ordering helper and the Observatory's distinct-source breadth; the signed evidence export is excluded by the ruling.
